1 · Intro

When to use it.

Non-exempt pay depends on approved time cards. This course shows how to find your employees, check their status, and act on a time card.

In UKG the order is: the employee approves, the manager approves, then payroll signs off before payroll runs.

Use this whenYou are checking or approving non-exempt hours for a pay period.

2 · Walk through

Step by step.

Follow along in UKG. Check off each step as you go.

Before you approve

The same four checks on every pay-impacting transaction. Draft: the owner for this area confirms anything marked To confirm.

Attach

None. The approved time card is the record.

Check

  • Exceptions such as a missing punch are resolved before you approve.
  • You are in the completed pay period, not the open one.
  • Hours and pay codes match what the employee worked.
  • You did not submit this time card yourself. The person who submits a time card does not approve it.

To confirmPayroll to confirm the rule on who approves, and who approves when the manager is out.

Cutoff

Weekly and biweekly pay: time cards must be approved before payroll signs off. The deadline is on the payroll calendar. After sign-off, an approval can't be removed unless payroll removes the sign-off first.

Who does what

  • Who starts it: The employee approves their own time card first.
  • Who approves: The manager approves. Payroll signs off.
  • What happens next: Payroll pays the approved hours.

Watch-outs

  • Empty time cards early in an open period are normal.
  • In an open period, Save. Don't Submit. Submitting means you must edit, update, and resubmit later.
  • Once payroll signs off a time card, an approval can't be removed unless the sign-off is removed first.
  • One person does not both submit and approve the same time card. If you submit a time card for an employee, the manager approves it, not you.
  • Open item: Payroll to confirm the rule that the person who submits a time card does not approve it, and who approves when the manager is out.

Official documentation

Vendor documentation describes the standard process. Vanderbilt's setup, codes, and rules in this course take priority.

  • UKG: Timecard approvals for managers (opens in a new tab)
  • UKG: Work with pay codes in the hourly timecard (opens in a new tab)

HCM Academy job aid · Payroll & Timecards

Review and approve time cards

Use when: You are checking or approving non-exempt hours for a pay period. · System: UKG (Kronos)

  1. Open UKG from Oracle.
  2. Open the time cards for your employees.
    • Filter: in the row under the column headings, type your business unit under Business Unit (or your work unit under Work Unit), then select Refresh. Until you filter, the list shows everyone you have access to.
    • Each row shows the Approval State: Open, Submitted, or Approved (PayPrep Ready).
  3. Review each employee's status and hours.
  4. To check the open period, move to the current pay period.
  5. Act on a time card.
    • Approve: the hours are correct and ready for payroll.
    • Submit on their behalf: the employee couldn't submit. Then the manager approves, not you.
    • Reject: send it back so it can be corrected.
  6. To enter hours for an employee, add a row on their time card and click Save.
    • In an open period, Save only. Don't submit.
  7. Confirm the result.

Before you approve

  • Attach: None. The approved time card is the record.
  • Check: Exceptions such as a missing punch are resolved before you approve. You are in the completed pay period, not the open one. Hours and pay codes match what the employee worked. You did not submit this time card yourself. The person who submits a time card does not approve it.
  • Cutoff: Approved before payroll signs off. The deadline is on the payroll calendar.

Watch-outs

  • Empty time cards early in an open period are normal.
  • In an open period, Save. Don't Submit. Submitting means you must edit, update, and resubmit later.
  • Once payroll signs off a time card, an approval can't be removed unless the sign-off is removed first.
  • One person does not both submit and approve the same time card. If you submit a time card for an employee, the manager approves it, not you.
  • Open item: Payroll to confirm the rule that the person who submits a time card does not approve it, and who approves when the manager is out.
